import androidx.room.Entity

/**
 * A speaker enrolled by the user in v2: a name plus the
 * speaker-embedding vector (a [ByteArray] of little-endian
 * float32, see [EmbeddingCodec]) the diarizer emits for a
 * short voice sample. Enrolled rows are global — they are not
 * scoped to a session, so the same enrollment is reused across
 * every recording.
 *
 * The unique index on [name] is what makes
 * [EnrolledSpeakerDao.upsertByName] safe: saving the same
 * `name` twice replaces the existing row's [embedding] /
 * [createdAt] without producing duplicates.
 */
@Entity(
    tableName = "enrolled_speakers",
    indices = [Index(value = ["name"], unique = true)]
)
data class EnrolledSpeakerEntity(
    @PrimaryKey(autoGenerate = true) val id: Long = 0,
    val name: String,
    val embedding: ByteArray,
    val createdAt: Long
) {
    /**
     * [ByteArray] equality is reference-based, which would make
     * Room emit spurious "row changed" notifications when the
     * embedding is reassigned. We compare contents instead so
     * two rows with the same name + same floats collapse to
     * `equals` and a replacement shows up as a real change.
     */
    override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean {
        if (this === other) return true
        if (other !is EnrolledSpeakerEntity) return false
        if (id != other.id) return false
        if (name != other.name) return false
        if (!embedding.contentEquals(other.embedding)) return false
        if (createdAt != other.createdAt) return false
        return true
    }

    override fun hashCode(): Int {
        var result = id.hashCode()
        result = 31 * result + name.hashCode()
        result = 31 * result + embedding.contentHashCode()
        result = 31 * result + createdAt.hashCode()
        return result
    }
}

     * Directory that holds every file for [bundle]. Created lazily by
     * the downloader; this class does not create it.
     */
    fun bundleDir(bundle: ModelBundle): File = File(root, bundle.id)

    /**
     * Absolute path to a single file inside [bundle]'s directory.
     * `fileName` may contain a sub-directory (e.g. `test_wavs/0.wav`).
     */
    fun fileFor(bundle: ModelBundle, fileName: String): File = File(bundleDir(bundle), fileName)

    /**
     * True iff every file declared in [bundle] is present on disk and
     * has exactly the expected [ModelFile.sizeBytes]. A zero-byte file
     * (interrupted download) is *not* considered installed.
     */
    fun isInstalled(bundle: ModelBundle): Boolean = bundle.files.all { file ->
        val onDisk = fileFor(bundle, file.fileName)
        onDisk.exists() && onDisk.length() == file.sizeBytes
    }

    /**
     * Bundles in [bundles] that are not fully installed, in input order.
     * The downloader uses this to decide what to fetch.
     */
    fun missing(bundles: List<ModelBundle>): List<ModelBundle> = bundles.filterNot(::isInstalled)

    /**
     * Remove every file of [bundle] from disk. Missing bundles are a
     * no-op. Used by the Settings screen to free space.
     */
    fun delete(bundle: ModelBundle) {
        val dir = bundleDir(bundle)
        if (dir.exists()) {
            dir.deleteRecursively()
        }
    }
}

package com.convoscribe.data

import java.nio.ByteBuffer
import java.nio.ByteOrder

/**
 * Convert between [FloatArray] speaker embeddings and the
 * little-endian float32 byte arrays Room stores on disk.
 *
 * The embedding model (WeSpeaker ResNet34, 256-dim) ships a
 * `FloatArray` whose length is fixed by the model. The database
 * needs raw bytes (Room's supported primitives do not include
 * `FloatArray`), so we go through a [ByteBuffer] in native byte
 * order. The conversion is symmetric: bytes → floats uses the
 * same order and the byte length is always `4 * size`, so a
 * corrupted row will fail loudly with a [java.nio.BufferUnderflowException]
 * instead of silently producing nonsense cosine scores.
 */

/**
 * Bytes per single-precision float. Pulled out as a constant
 * so the conversion can be inverted to a `FloatArray` size
 * without a magic number.
 */
const val EMBEDDING_FLOAT_BYTES: Int = 4

/**
 * Pack [this] as little-endian float32. The resulting array's
 * length is `size * [EMBEDDING_FLOAT_BYTES]`.
 */
fun FloatArray.toBytes(): ByteArray {
    val buf = ByteBuffer.allocate(size * EMBEDDING_FLOAT_BYTES).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN)
    buf.asFloatBuffer().put(this)
    return buf.array()
}

/**
 * Unpack a little-endian float32 [ByteArray] into a
 * [FloatArray]. The byte length must be a multiple of
 * [EMBEDDING_FLOAT_BYTES]; otherwise the [ByteBuffer] will
 * throw a [java.nio.BufferUnderflowException] at read time,
 * which is the correct loud-failure behaviour for a corrupt row.
 */
fun ByteArray.toFloats(): FloatArray {
    val floats = FloatArray(size / EMBEDDING_FLOAT_BYTES)
    ByteBuffer.wrap(this).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).asFloatBuffer().get(floats)
    return floats
}
